title.narrative: Denmark’s Core Voluntary Contributions to the World Health Organisation in 2024-2028

description.narrative:
The World Health Organization (WHO) is the United Nations agency for health responsible for setting evidence based global technical norms and standards, monitoring global health trends and providing policy options and assistance to member states. Denmark’s voluntary contributions to WHO are made within the framework of Danish Organisation Strategy for World Health Organisation (WHO) 2024-2028.
The overall objective of Denmark’s support is to contribute to the achievement of the health related United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), in particular SDG 3 (good health and well-being), 5 (gender equality), 10 reduced inequalities, and 17 (partnership for the goals).
Four priority areas have been chosen based on the WHO Programme of Work: 1. Health systems strengthening to achieve universal health coverage; 2. Pandemic, health emergencies and global health risk preparedness; 3. Human rights and gender equality, including sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR); and 4. A more effective and efficient WHO, that also contributes to the efficiency reform efforts of the United Nations Development System.
